nodes.label: desktop memory - code readability and plain naming

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. When the user reads code, unreadability is a real defect to him, voiced bluntly as code-cancer, 90% jargon and everything named alike. Concretely he objects to jargon-dense or over-long comments; multiple symbols named so similarly they blur (_MIN_INTERVAL_S against RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN against _WINDOW_S); a comment that distinguishes one thing from a near-identical other; and dead or redundant machinery left in place. Comments and names feed the graph and memory and get re-read every session, so unclear code compounds, and he hunts for a specific knob such as seconds between calls while alike-named symbols make it un-findable. Use plain descriptive names a reader greps for directly (SECONDS_BETWEEN_CALLS, not _MIN_INTERVAL_S); one short plain-English comment, not five jargon lines; collapse two overlapping mechanisms into one when one is dead at the real config; and fix a misleading comment to state what the code actually does. CANON_AUDIT.md lists this among the grounded, verbatim-quoted and correct desktop entries
